design_brief: The xandra-roll-offs module has a solid functional foundation with a condensed dark visual system, but the UX layer exhibits hierarchy confusion, affordance gaps, accessibility shortcomings, and responsive fragility. The GM setup flow exists in two divergent forms (GMPanelApp vs RollOffWindow empty state), session history is buried behind a title-bar toggle with no discoverability, the ApplicationV2 title-bar control ordering has been iteratively patched but remains brittle, and round-row horizontal navigation relies on hover-revealed chevrons that fail keyboard/touch users. The current compact single-screen setup in RollOffWindow is the stronger pattern but needs elevation to a dedicated setup mode; GMPanelApp should be deprecated or merged. Priority fixes: unify setup into a single authoritative flow with progressive disclosure, promote history to a first-class nav target, stabilize title-bar integration via native ApplicationV2 controls, and replace hover-dependent row navigation with persistent, keyboard-accessible controls.

priorities.problem: Two divergent GM setup flows (GMPanelApp checkbox form vs RollOffWindow avatar-row picker) create inconsistent mental models, duplicated logic, and maintenance burden. GMPanelApp uses a legacy form pattern with checkboxes in a scroll list; RollOffWindow uses a modern avatar-row selection with aria-pressed/keyboard support, setup summary, and icon-supported rule fields. Neither is a true wizard — both are single-screen but RollOffWindow's is more condensed and accessible.
priorities.recommendation: Consolidate into a single authoritative setup flow in RollOffWindow (deprecate GMPanelApp or make it a thin launcher). Adopt a compact single-screen layout with progressive disclosure: 1) Participant selection as the primary action (avatar rows, multi-select, keyboard accessible), 2) Rules configuration (die type, wins needed) as a secondary collapsible section with smart defaults, 3) Start button disabled until ≥2 participants selected. Do NOT use a multi-step wizard — the decision space is small (3-4 inputs), users are typically GMs under time pressure, and a single screen preserves context. Add a 'Save as default' affordance for repeated setups.

priorities.problem: Session history is accessible only via a title-bar toggle button (clock icon) with no label in the default state, no keyboard shortcut, and no entry point from the empty state or GM panel. The toggle uses aria-pressed but lacks a visible label when not hovered, failing WCAG 2.1 2.5.3 (Label in Name) and 2.4.7 (Focus Visible). History view itself has no 'back' affordance other than the same toggle.
priorities.recommendation: Promote history to a first-class navigation element: 1) Add a persistent 'History' tab/button in the window's primary chrome (alongside the title), not buried in the title-bar controls. 2) In the empty state, show a 'Recent Sessions' summary row (latest 3) with a 'View all' link. 3) Ensure the history view has an explicit close/back button with aria-label. 4) Add keyboard shortcut (e.g., Ctrl/Cmd+H) and register it in Foundry's hotkey system. 5) Make the title-bar toggle a secondary access point only, with a visible text label ('History') not just an icon.

priorities.problem: Round-row horizontal navigation uses floating chevron buttons that are hidden until JS measures overflow (visibility: hidden when not scrollable), have no keyboard operability, rely on hover for discovery, and provide no touch-friendly hit targets. The row uses scroll-snap but no scroll-snap-type, and chevrons scroll by a fixed 72% of viewport — arbitrary and not aligned to pill boundaries. On narrow windows (<420px), pills are clipped with no indication of hidden content.
priorities.recommendation: Redesign round-row navigation as a persistent, accessible pattern: 1) Always-visible chevron buttons (opacity 0.4 when at scroll limits, not display:none) with min 44x44px touch targets. 2) Add keyboard support: Left/Right arrows when row is focused (roving tabindex on pills), Home/End for jump. 3) Use scroll-snap-type: x mandatory on the row and scroll-snap-align: center on pills so chevron clicks snap to pill centers. 4) Add a scroll-shadow gradient fade on the left/right edges of the scroller as a persistent visual affordance of hidden content. 5) On mobile/narrow viewports, enable native touch-drag scrolling (already works) but ensure chevrons don't obstruct pills.

priorities.problem: ApplicationV2 title-bar control ordering has been patched 8+ times (per progress.md) and remains brittle: History button insertion depends on runtime DOM queries against Foundry's internal .window-controls/.window-header-controls structure, which can change between versions. The current order (title → History → menu → Close) was achieved by swapping DOM nodes post-render — a fragile approach that breaks if Foundry reorders native controls.
priorities.recommendation: Use ApplicationV2's native `controls` array in DEFAULT_OPTIONS (as already defined for the History button) and let Foundry handle ordering. Remove all runtime DOM injection/swapping code in _onRender. If native ordering doesn't match the desired sequence, use CSS `order` properties on the control elements within the .window-header-controls flex container. This delegates layout to the browser's flexbox and survives Foundry updates. Verify the control renders with the correct `data-action="toggleHistory"` and `aria-pressed` binding.

priorities.problem: Visual hierarchy in the active roll-off view is flat: round history, current round, win tracker, and footer actions all share similar container styling (rounded borders, same background). The 'current round' group has a subtle blue accent but no structural differentiation. The win tracker uses a checkbox-hack collapse pattern that is not keyboard accessible (no role=button, no aria-expanded). The footer action buttons change context (Roll → Next Round → Close) but occupy the same visual slot without clear state signaling.
priorities.recommendation: Establish a clear 3-layer hierarchy: 1) **Round Stack** (scrollable history + current round) as the primary content surface — single shared container with top-rounded corners. 2) **Win Tracker** as a secondary, collapsible panel — replace checkbox hack with a <button aria-expanded> toggle, animate height, keep collapsed by default showing only current user's row. 3) **Action Bar** as a fixed footer — use semantic button variants (primary: Roll/Next Round, danger: Cancel/Close) with consistent width and clear disabled states. Add a subtle separator (hairline) between layers. Current round should have a persistent 'LIVE' badge, not just a title suffix.

priorities.problem: Responsive behavior is undefined below the default 420px window width. The participant pills (82px fixed) + avatar + value badge + name truncate aggressively. The setup summary (die · wins) wraps awkwardly. The title-bar controls collide with the window title. No breakpoint strategy exists for tablet/narrow desktop contexts common in Foundry's sidebar-docked windows.
priorities.recommendation: Define two responsive breakpoints: 1) **≤380px (narrow/sidebar dock)**: Pills shrink to 68px, names truncate at 8chars, avatar 24px, value badge only (no name), chevrons become 36px touch targets, setup summary stacks vertically, title-bar controls drop icon-only labels. 2) **≥600px (wide)**: Show full names, expand tracker by default, show round timestamps. Implement via CSS container queries on .xandra-roll-offs-window (not viewport media queries) so behavior adapts to the window's actual size in Foundry's multi-window environment. Test at 320px, 380px, 420px, 500px, 600px.

priorities.problem: The empty state (no active roll-off) shows 'No active roll-off' notice but provides no onboarding for new GMs — no hint that this is where roll-offs start, no template presets, no recent-config recall. The participant list shows all users but no filtering (online/offline, GM/players). The setup summary shows defaults but doesn't indicate they're editable until interacted with.
priorities.recommendation: Add lightweight onboarding to the empty state: 1) A one-line hint: 'Select participants, choose die & wins, click Start'. 2) Add a filter chip row above participant list: [All] [Online] [Players] [GM]. 3) Make the setup summary visually distinct (card-like) with a subtle edit affordance (pencil icon on hover) to signal interactivity. 4) Add a 'Recent configurations' dropdown (last 3 used die/wins/participant combos) as a progressive enhancement — only if localStorage/sessionStorage permits. Keep it under 3 lines of additional UI.

priorities.problem: Accessibility gaps across the module: Participant rows in setup use role=button + aria-pressed but are not in a <fieldset>/<legend> group; no announcement of selection count. History toggle lacks visible label. Win tracker toggle is a checkbox hack (not a button). Round pills have no role (should be listitem in a list). Chat cards (outside this review scope but related) use color-only winner indication (green border) without text/icon backup.
priorities.recommendation: Targeted accessibility fixes: 1) Wrap participant selection in <fieldset><legend>Participants</legend> with a live region announcing 'X of Y selected'. 2) Convert win tracker toggle to <button aria-expanded aria-controls="tracker-rows">. 3) Make round history a <ol> with <li role="listitem"> for each round. 4) Add winner icon (trophy) + text 'Winner' to round pills, not just color. 5) Ensure all interactive elements meet 44x44px minimum (chevrons, pill roll buttons, avatar click targets). 6) Test with NVDA/JAWS + Foundry's screen reader mode.

priorities.problem: Session history view renders each session as an article with a header (winner, timestamp), meta line, and round grid. The round grid uses a 3-column layout (label, winner, value) that collapses poorly on narrow widths — winner name truncates, value badge wraps. No visual distinction between regular rounds and tiebreaks beyond a warning-colored label. No session-level actions (re-run, export, delete).
priorities.recommendation: Redesign session history items as responsive cards: 1) Stack vertically on <400px: winner banner full-width, meta as chips, rounds as a scrollable row of pill cards (same .xro-roll-pill pattern). 2) Tiebreak rounds get a distinct '⚡ Tie' badge + amber accent, not just label color. 3) Add a session action menu (⋮) with 'Re-run with same settings', 'Export JSON', 'Remove from history' (GM only). 4) Show participant avatars in the session header (max 5, +N overflow). 5) Use the same scroll-shadow affordance as round rows for horizontal round browsing.
